Amr ibn al-As.fact: In the following month, his army decisively defeated the Byzantines at the Battle of Heliopolis.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He captured _____ soon after and besieged Babylon
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He captured Memphis soon after and besieged Babylon.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the _____-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople
Amr ibn al-As.fact: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the Alexandria-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople. Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr made an agreement with the _____ garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641
Amr ibn al-As.fact: During the siege, Amr entered truce negotiations with the Alexandria-based Byzantine governor Cyrus; Emperor Heraclius opposed the talks and recalled Cyrus to Constantinople. Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Though strong resistance was put up by _____'s defenders, their morale was sapped after news of Heraclius' death in February 641
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He captured Memphis soon after and besieged Babylon. Though strong resistance was put up by Babylon's defenders, their morale was sapped after news of Heraclius' death in February 641.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: One of them, _____ ibn Hudhafa, captured the Fayyum oasis, Oxyrhynchus (Bahnasa), Hermopolis (el-Ashmunein) and Akhmim, all in Middle Egypt, and an unspecified number of villages in Upper Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: One of them, Kharija ibn Hudhafa, captured the Fayyum oasis, Oxyrhynchus (Bahnasa), Hermopolis (el-Ashmunein) and Akhmim, all in Middle Egypt, and an unspecified number of villages in Upper Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In late 641, Amr besieged _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr made an agreement with the Byzantine garrison, allowing their peaceful withdrawal toward the provincial capital Alexandria on 9 April 641. In late 641, Amr besieged Alexandria.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The date of the city's surrender was likely _____ 642
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The date of the city's surrender was likely November 642.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security

Amr ibn al-As.fact: Taking advantage of the uncertain political situation in the wake of Umar's death in 644 and the meager Arab military presence in Alexandria, Emperor Constans II (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 641–668) dispatched a naval expedition led by a certain _____ which occupied the city and killed most of its Arab garrison in 645
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 641–668) dispatched a naval expedition led by a certain Manuel which occupied the city and killed most of its Arab garrison in 645. He besieged and captured Alexandria in the summer of 646; most of the Byzantines, including Manuel, were slain, many of its inhabitants were killed and the city was burned until Amr ordered an end to the onslaught.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Byzantine forces pushed deeper into the _____, but Amr forced them back at the Battle of Nikiou
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Byzantine forces pushed deeper into the Nile Delta, but Amr forced them back at the Battle of Nikiou.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Afterward, Muslim rule in _____ was gradually solidified
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Alexandria's elite and most of the inhabitants assisted the Byzantines; medieval Byzantine, Coptic and, to a lesser extent, Muslim sources indicate the city was not firmly in Arab hands during the preceding three years. He besieged and captured Alexandria in the summer of 646; most of the Byzantines, including Manuel, were slain, many of its inhabitants were killed and the city was burned until Amr ordered an end to the onslaught.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In the absence of siege engines, Amr oversaw long sieges of heavily fortified _____ positions, most prominently Babylon, cut supply lines and engaged in long wars of attrition
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In contrast to the disarray of the Byzantine defense, the Muslim forces under Amr's command were unified and organized; Amr frequently coordinated with Caliph Umar and his own troops for all major military decisions. According to the historian Vassilios Christides, Amr "cautiously counterbalanced the superiority in numbers and equipment of the Byzantine army by applying skillful military tactics" and despite the lack of "definite, prepared, long-term plans, the Arab army moved with great flex...

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: His cavalry-dominated army moved through _____'s deserts and oases with relative ease
Amr ibn al-As.fact: His cavalry-dominated army moved through Egypt's deserts and oases with relative ease.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Moreover, political circumstances became more favorable to Amr with the death of the hawkish _____ and his short-term replacement with the more pacifist Heraklonas and Martina.
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Moreover, political circumstances became more favorable to Amr with the death of the hawkish Heraclius and his short-term replacement with the more pacifist Heraklonas and Martina.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Toward the end of the year, Amr launched a second cavalry assault targeting _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Toward the end of the year, Amr launched a second cavalry assault targeting Tripoli. After about a month, his troops entered Tripoli through a vulnerable point in its walls and sacked the city.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After about a month, his troops entered _____ through a vulnerable point in its walls and sacked the city
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Toward the end of the year, Amr launched a second cavalry assault targeting Tripoli. After about a month, his troops entered Tripoli through a vulnerable point in its walls and sacked the city.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The city was heavily fortified by the _____ and contained several naval vessels in its harbor
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The city was heavily fortified by the Byzantines and contained several naval vessels in its harbor.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Due to his lack of siege engines, he employed the lengthy siege tactic used in the _____ conquest
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Due to his lack of siege engines, he employed the lengthy siege tactic used in the Egyptian conquest.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Its fall, which entailed the evacuation by sea of the _____ garrison and most of the population, is dated to 642 or 643/44
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The city was heavily fortified by the Byzantines and contained several naval vessels in its harbor. Its fall, which entailed the evacuation by sea of the Byzantine garrison and most of the population, is dated to 642 or 643/44.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The region was definitively conquered by the Arabs during the reign of _____ al-Malik (r
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The region was definitively conquered by the Arabs during the reign of Caliph Abd al-Malik (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: During his siege of _____, Amr had erected an encampment near the fortress
Amr ibn al-As.fact: During his siege of Babylon, Amr had erected an encampment near the fortress. Instead, following Alexandria's surrender, in 641 or 642, Amr made his encampment near Babylon the permanent garrison town (miṣr) of Fustat, the first town set up by the Arabs in Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He originally intended for _____ to serve as the Arabs' capital in Egypt, but Umar rejected this on the basis that no body of water, i.e
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He originally intended for Alexandria to serve as the Arabs' capital in Egypt, but Umar rejected this on the basis that no body of water, i.e. Instead, following Alexandria's surrender, in 641 or 642, Amr made his encampment near Babylon the permanent garrison town (miṣr) of Fustat, the first town set up by the Arabs in Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Instead, following _____'s surrender, in 641 or 642, Amr made his encampment near Babylon the permanent garrison town (miṣr) of Fustat, the first town founded by the Arabs in Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He originally intended for Alexandria to serve as the Arabs' capital in Egypt, but Umar rejected this on the basis that no body of water, i.e. Instead, following Alexandria's surrender, in 641 or 642, Amr made his encampment near Babylon the permanent garrison town (miṣr) of Fustat, the first town set up by the Arabs in Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: the _____, should separate the caliph from his army
Amr ibn al-As.fact: the Nile, should separate the caliph from his army. Its location along the eastern bank of the Nile River and at the head of the Nile Delta and edge of the Eastern Desert strategically positioned it to dominate the Upper and Lower halves of Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Its location along the eastern bank of the _____ and at the head of the Nile Delta and edge of the Eastern Desert strategically positioned it to dominate the Upper and Lower halves of Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Its location along the eastern bank of the Nile River and at the head of the Nile Delta and edge of the Eastern Desert strategically positioned it to dominate the Upper and Lower halves of Egypt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr had the original tents of _____ replaced with mud brick and baked brick dwellings
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Instead, following Alexandria's surrender, in 641 or 642, Amr made his encampment near Babylon the permanent garrison town (miṣr) of Fustat, the first town set up by the Arabs in Egypt. Fustat's proximity to Babylon, where Amr also set up an Arab garrison, afforded the Arab settlers a convenient means to employ and oversee the Coptic bureaucratic officials who inhabited Babylon and proved critical to running the day-to-day affairs of the Arab government.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Documents found in _____ (al-Ashmunayn) dating from the 640s confirm official orders to forward building materials to Babylon to construct the new city
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Documents found in Hermopolis (al-Ashmunayn) dating from the 640s confirm official orders to forward building materials to Babylon to construct the new city.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The city was organized into allotments over an area stretching 5–6 kilometers (3.1–3.7 mi) along the _____ and 1–2 kilometers (0.62–1.24 mi) inland to the east
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The city was organized into allotments over an area stretching 5–6 kilometers (3.1–3.7 mi) along the Nile and 1–2 kilometers (0.62–1.24 mi) inland to the east.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: This part of the city became the administrative and social core of Arab settlement in _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In the northwestern part of Alexandria, Amr built a hilltop congregational mosque, later called after him, before the Byzantine occupation of 645/46, after which he built a second called the Mosque of Mercy; neither mosque has been presently identified. This part of the city became the administrative and social core of Arab settlement in Alexandria.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: As per the 641 treaty with Cyrus, Amr imposed a poll tax of two gold dinars on non-_____ adult males
Amr ibn al-As.fact: As per the 641 treaty with Cyrus, Amr imposed a poll tax of two gold dinars on non-Muslim adult males. After taking a census of the Muslims, he further ordered that each Muslim be annually supplied by the inhabitants a highly embroidered wool robe (Egyptian robes were prized by the Arabs), a burnous, a turban, a sirwal (trousers) and shoes.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He imposed other measures, sanctioned by _____, that entailed the inhabitants' regular provision of wheat, honey, oil and vinegar as a subsistence allowance for the Arab troops
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He imposed other measures, sanctioned by Umar, that entailed the inhabitants' regular provision of wheat, honey, oil and vinegar as a subsistence allowance for the Arab troops.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After entering _____, Amr invited the Coptic patriarch Benjamin to return to the city after his years of exile under Cyrus
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After entering Alexandria, Amr invited the Coptic patriarch Benjamin to return to the city after his years of exile under Cyrus.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The patriarch maintained close ties with Amr and restored the monasteries of Wadi al-Natrun, including the _____, which functions until the present-day
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The patriarch maintained close ties with Amr and restored the monasteries of Wadi al-Natrun, including the Saint Macarius Monastery, which functions until the present-day.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: According to the historian _____, "Benjamin played a major role in the survival of the Coptic Church through the transition to Arab rule"
Amr ibn al-As.fact: According to the historian Hugh N. Kennedy, "Benjamin played a major role in the survival of the Coptic Church through the transition to Arab rule".

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He also amassed significant personal wealth in Egypt, part of which was confiscated by _____ ibn Maslama on Umar's orders
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He also amassed significant personal wealth in Egypt, part of which was confiscated by Muhammad ibn Maslama on Umar's orders.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: At a certain point, the _____ separated Upper Egypt from Amr's administration and appointed Abd Allah ibn Sa'd over the region
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At a certain point, the Caliph separated Upper Egypt from Amr's administration and appointed Abd Allah ibn Sa'd over the region. Umar's successor Caliph Uthman (r.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 644–656) initially kept Amr in his governorship and forged marital links with him by wedding to him his maternal half-sister _____ bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 644–656) initially kept Amr in his governorship and forged marital links with him by wedding to him his maternal half-sister Umm Kulthum bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Uthman diluted Amr's power in 645/46 by transferring fiscal responsibilities to _____, his own relative, leaving Amr in charge of military affairs
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Uthman diluted Amr's power in 645/46 by transferring fiscal responsibilities to Ibn Abi Sarh, his own relative, leaving Amr in charge of military affairs.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr and _____'d lodged complaints to Uthman each alleging the other of incompetence, prompting Uthman to dismiss Amr entirely and replace him in his duties with Ibn Sa'd
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr and Ibn Sa'd lodged complaints to Uthman each alleging the other of incompetence, prompting Uthman to dismiss Amr entirely and replace him in his duties with Ibn Sa'd. Ibn Sa'd reduced the fiscal privileges of Egypt's original Arab military settlers, who had been shown favor by Amr, and secured the remittance of the surplus to Medina.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Open opposition to _____'d and Uthman began under the leadership of the Qurayshite Muhammad ibn Abi Hudhayfa in 654/55
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Ibn Sa'd reduced the fiscal privileges of Egypt's original Arab military settlers, who had been shown favor by Amr, and secured the remittance of the surplus to Medina. Open opposition to Ibn Sa'd and Uthman began under the leadership of the Qurayshite Muhammad ibn Abi Hudhayfa in 654/55.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He lobbied _____'s wife A'isha for support and the latter pressed Uthman to reappoint Amr to Egypt citing its garrisons' satisfaction with his rule
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Open opposition to Ibn Sa'd and Uthman began under the leadership of the Qurayshite Muhammad ibn Abi Hudhayfa in 654/55. The caliph and Amr engaged in a number of heated public exchanges and, according to a report in the Islamic traditional sources, Amr incited Muhammad's senior companions Ali, Zubayr and Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, as well as the Hajj pilgrims in Mecca, against Uthman.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After his last exchange with _____, Amr retired to his estate in southern Palestine
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In a sermon at the mosque in Medina in June 656 and a letter penned to the Muslim leaders in Syria, Uthman mentioned that he had intended to reappoint Amr but did not follow through as a result of the latter's excessive insult. According to the historian Wilferd Madelung, the insult Uthman cited was likely Amr's public reaction to the caliph's statement that the mutinous Egyptian troops who had arrived in Medina to protest the Caliph's policies had withdrawn because they were misinformed: "Fe...

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: 892) and Yaqut al-_____ (d
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 892) and Yaqut al-Hamawi (d.

Amr ibn al-As.question: _____) also suggest that Ajlan was located in the area of Bayt Jibrin
Amr ibn al-As.fact: 1226) also suggest that Ajlan was in the area of Bayt Jibrin.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: He lived on the estate, where he derived agricultural revenue, with his sons Muhammad and _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: He lived on the estate, where he derived agricultural revenue, with his sons Muhammad and Abd Allah.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: At his estate Amr received news of the siege of _____'s house and the caliph's subsequent assassination by Amr's Egyptian partisans
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At his estate Amr received news of the siege of Uthman's house and the caliph's subsequent assassination by Amr's Egyptian partisans. The roughly 400–600 Egyptian mutineers had protested Uthman's fiscal centralization policies in Medina and accused him of favoring his relatives over the early Muslim converts.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The roughly 400–600 _____ mutineers had protested Uthman's fiscal centralization policies in Medina and accused him of favoring his relatives over the early Muslim converts
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At his estate Amr received news of the siege of Uthman's house and the caliph's subsequent assassination by Amr's Egyptian partisans. The roughly 400–600 Egyptian mutineers had protested Uthman's fiscal centralization policies in Medina and accused him of favoring his relatives over the early Muslim converts.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The caliph had initially persuaded them to withdraw, but when they intercepted a letter on their departure ordering _____ to punish them, they turned back and assaulted Uthman in his home
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The caliph had initially persuaded them to withdraw, but when they intercepted a letter on their departure ordering Ibn Abi Sarh to punish them, they turned back and assaulted Uthman in his home.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In an anecdote cited by al-_____, Amr is quoted as taking partial credit for Uthman's assassination
Amr ibn al-As.fact: In an anecdote cited by al-Baladhuri, Amr is quoted as taking partial credit for Uthman's assassination.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Ali succeeded _____, but did not reappoint Amr to his post in Egypt
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The roughly 400–600 Egyptian mutineers had protested Uthman's fiscal centralization policies in Medina and accused him of favoring his relatives over the early Muslim converts. The caliph had initially persuaded them to withdraw, but when they intercepted a letter on their departure ordering Ibn Abi Sarh to punish them, they turned back and assaulted Uthman in his home.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Nonetheless the governor of Syria, which included Palestine, the _____'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, had left Amr on his estate undisturbed
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Nonetheless the governor of Syria, which included Palestine, the Umayyad Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, had left Amr on his estate undisturbed.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: In the ensuing negotiations, Amr pressed Mu'awiya for lifetime possession of Egypt, to which Mu'awiya ultimately acceded after being persuaded by his brother Utba ibn _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Nonetheless the governor of Syria, which included Palestine, the Umayyad Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, had left Amr on his estate undisturbed. In the ensuing negotiations, Amr pressed Mu'awiya for lifetime possession of Egypt, to which Mu'awiya ultimately acceded after being persuaded by his brother Utba ibn Abi Sufyan.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The public agreement, composed by Amr's mawlā Wardan and made in _____, secured Amr's allegiance to Mu'awiya in return for the latter's assistance in gaining control of Egypt from Ali's governor
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The public agreement, composed by Amr's mawlā Wardan and made in Jerusalem, secured Amr's allegiance to Mu'awiya in return for the latter's assistance in gaining control of Egypt from Ali's governor.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: According to _____, the "alliance between Mu'awiya and Amr b
Amr ibn al-As.fact: According to Madelung, the "alliance between Mu'awiya and Amr b.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr then advised Mu'awiya to lead the _____ army in person against Ali, who began his march toward Syria in late May 657
Amr ibn al-As.fact: To secure the defense of his Syrian realm from Ali's loyalists in Egypt, Amr counseled Mu'awiya to secure the support of the Judhamite chief in Palestine, Natil ibn Qays, by ignoring his seizure of the district treasury; Natil subsequently joined Mu'awiya's cause. Amr then advised Mu'awiya to lead the Syrian army in person against Ali, who began his march toward Syria in late May 657.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: After Ali protested, Amr advised Mu'awiya to accept their request as preventing access to water might rally the hitherto demotivated Iraqis to a determined fight against the _____
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After Ali protested, Amr advised Mu'awiya to accept their request as preventing access to water might rally the hitherto demotivated Iraqis to a determined fight against the Syrians. Mu'awiya refused and the Iraqis subsequently defeated the Syrians led by Amr and Abu al-A'war in a skirmish called the "Day of the Euphrates".

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Mu'awiya refused and the _____ subsequently defeated the Syrians led by Amr and Abu al-A'war in a skirmish known as the "Day of the Euphrates"
Amr ibn al-As.fact: After Ali protested, Amr advised Mu'awiya to accept their request as preventing access to water might rally the hitherto demotivated Iraqis to a determined fight against the Syrians. Mu'awiya refused and the Iraqis subsequently defeated the Syrians led by Amr and Abu al-A'war in a skirmish called the "Day of the Euphrates".

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: At one point in the battle, he raised a black fabric given to him by _____ at the tip of his spear, symbolizing the command role given to him by Muhammad
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At one point in the battle, he raised a black fabric given to him by Muhammad at the tip of his spear, symbolizing the command role given to him by Muhammad.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The Caliph heeded the majority will in his army to settle the matter diplomatically; an arbitration was agreed with Amr representing Mu'awiya and _____ al-Ash'ari representing Ali
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The Caliph heeded the majority will in his army to settle the matter diplomatically; an arbitration was agreed with Amr representing Mu'awiya and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari representing Ali. Amr and Abu Musa likely met twice, at Dumat al-Jandal and then Adhruh, to forge an agreement.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr and _____ likely met twice, at Dumat al-Jandal and then Adhruh, to forge an agreement
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The Caliph heeded the majority will in his army to settle the matter diplomatically; an arbitration was agreed with Amr representing Mu'awiya and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari representing Ali. Amr and Abu Musa likely met twice, at Dumat al-Jandal and then Adhruh, to forge an agreement.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The omission effectively placed Ali and Mu'awiya on an equal political footing and thereby weakened Ali's leadership position over the _____ polity
Amr ibn al-As.fact: The omission effectively placed Ali and Mu'awiya on an equal political footing and thereby weakened Ali's leadership position over the Muslim polity.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Abu Musa retired to Mecca, while Amr and the _____ returned to Mu'awiya and recognized him as amir al-mu'minin before formally pledging allegiance to him in April/May 658
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Abu Musa retired to Mecca, while Amr and the Syrians returned to Mu'awiya and recognized him as amir al-mu'minin before formally pledging allegiance to him in April/May 658.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: As a result, Amr was among those invoked in a ritual curse issued by Ali during the morning prayers and became the subject of derision among the _____ core of Ali's supporters
Amr ibn al-As.fact: At the last meeting in Adhruh, the office of the caliphate was discussed, but the meeting ended in violence and without agreement; during the brawl, Amr was physically assaulted by a Kufan partisan of Ali, but the latter was fended off by one of Amr's sons. As a result, Amr was among those invoked in a ritual curse issued by Ali during the morning prayers and became the subject of derision among the Kufan core of Ali's supporters.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Amr and Mu'awiya did not advance further than this point and _____ was executed
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Amr and Mu'awiya did not advance further than this point and Ibn Abi Hudhayfa was executed.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Malik's replacement was _____ ibn Abi Bakr, son of the first caliph and a foster son of Ali
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Malik's replacement was Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, son of the first caliph and a foster son of Ali.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: Ibn Abi Bakr burned the homes and arrested the families of pro-_____ mutineers from the Fustat garrison led by Mu'awiya ibn Hudayj and Maslama ibn Mukhallad
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Ibn Abi Bakr burned the homes and arrested the families of pro-Uthman mutineers from the Fustat garrison led by Mu'awiya ibn Hudayj and Maslama ibn Mukhallad.

Amr ibn al-As.subject: Defence & Security
Amr ibn al-As.question: The latter two requested intervention by Mu'awiya, who dispatched Amr to _____ with a 4,000–6,000-strong army
Amr ibn al-As.fact: Ali's second governor in Egypt, Qays ibn Sa'd, was dismissed in late 657 due to concerns that he would defect to Mu'awiya and his next appointee, Malik al-Ashtar, died in Qulzum (Suez) on his way to the province. Border Security Force.question: This attack exposed the inadequacy of the _____ in coping with armed aggression
Border Security Force.fact: BSF has been termed the First Line of Defence of Indian territories.  == History == Since India's independence in 1947, the protection of its international boundaries was the responsibility of the local police in each border state, with little inter-state coordination.  However, during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965, Pakistan attacked Sardar Post, Char Bet, and Beria Bet on 9 April 1965, in Kutch.  This attack exposed the inadequacy of the State Armed Police in coping with armed aggression.  Thus, after the war, the government created the Border Security Force as a unified central agency with the specific mandate of guarding India's international borders.  This act brought greater cohesion to border security.  K F Rustamji, from the Indian Police Service, was the first Director General of the BSF
